currentContext.business: Saksoft Limited delivers an integrated portfolio of digital transformation solutions spanning domain-driven technology solutions, strategic consulting, analytics, IoT and mobility, application development, robotic process automation, digital commerce, digital testing and technology training. It organises delivery around four industry practices - Banking & Financial Services, Logistics and Transportation, Digital Commerce, and Emerging Verticals (Telecom, Hi-Tech and Utilities) - selling to banks, fintechs, carriers, third-party logistics providers, ports and terminals, shippers, logistics ISVs, B2C/B2B/D2C brands and commerce ISVs. currentContext.strengths: Domain-led delivery with named vertical specialist pools - '400+ Logistics Domain Specialists', '900+ BFS and Fintech Specialists' and '300+ Specialists' in Digital Commerce|Proprietary accelerators and frameworks reused across engagements (SakMod, UNITE, SakCare, LEAP, Voice BOT, Helsinki, Oslo, Vue Storefront, Commerce Command Centre Framework), which the Company positions as reducing time-to-value and deepening its role in customer transformation journeys|Consistent operating fundamentals: the COO & CFO states utilisation levels 'have been consistent over the past several years' and attrition 'has remained broadly steady year on year', described as a meaningful competitive differentiator in an industry where talent is both primary asset and primary risk|Multi-geography delivery and client footprint (United States, Europe, Asia Pacific) enabling integrated, cross-border technology solutions|Acquisition philosophy framed around acquiring capabilities, talent and entrepreneurial leadership rather than bought revenue, preserving an entrepreneurial operating culture|Balance-sheet strength cited by the COO & CFO - the year closed with a net cash surplus and an interest coverage ratio in excess of 21 times
currentContext.strategies: Six Big Bets framing the next chapter: (1) AI-Powered Shared Services & Unified Command Centre Operations, (2) AI-Led ADMs & Vendor Consolidation, (3) Legacy Modernisation & AI-Readiness Transformation, (4) Autonomous QA Ops & AI-Led Quality Engineering, (5) AI-First Digital Engineering & Future Development Engineering (FDE), (6) DataOps, Data, AI & Security as a Service|Shift from execution-led engagements to broader transformation ownership - helping customers optimise current operating models while creating capacity for AI-led growth|Expand wallet share within existing accounts, strengthen customer ownership and account stickiness, and increase participation in larger multi-year transformation programmes|Improve the annuity and recurring revenue mix by expanding beyond project support into managed outcomes, managed assurance and enterprise operating-model engagements|Position Saksoft as an AI-first transformation and managed-outcomes partner, engaging customers early in operating-model evolution with AI-led delivery frameworks, SRE practices, DevOps and intelligent managed services|Build and monetise reusable AI-led accelerators as the source of differentiation - SakMod (enterprise modernisation), SakVerse (commerce/CX and QA), VoicePilot (agentic AI), DataOps AI Studio, Headless 360 and SakPilot (enterprise AI readiness)|Run Enterprise AI Competency Centres on a Build-Operate-Transfer model, embedding AI architects, data and platform engineers and AI governance expertise inside client organisations|Operationalise enterprise data and AI platforms on a DataOps-led Build / Run / Modernise model, with capability expanded across Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake, AWS, GCP and Lakehouse architectures|Operate the ServiceNow practice as a dedicated Centre of Excellence spanning ITSM, ITOM, ITAM, SPM, GRC, CSM, employee experience and AI-enabled workflow automation|Dividend is distributed under a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy, in two tranches during the year - an interim dividend declared by the Board and a final dividend recommended by the Board and put to shareholders at the AGM (for FY 2025-26 the AGM is asked to approve a final dividend of 55%, or Re. 0.55 per equity share, in addition to the interim of Re. 0.45 per share already paid). Unclaimed dividends and the related shares are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund once unclaimed for seven consecutive years, with a Nodal Officer appointed and claim details published on the Company's website, and shares under a specific court, tribunal or statutory-authority restraining order excluded. Note: the section routed to this reader under the header 'DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY' does not contain the policy itself - it contains the Corporate Governance Report's unclaimed-dividend / IEPF and unclaimed-suspense-account disclosures - so the policy's own payout parameters are not evidenced here.|A comprehensive ESG materiality analysis has been carried out, using stakeholder engagement and impact-based evaluation to identify and rank material topics; ten material issues are disclosed with rationale, mitigation approach and the direction of financial implication|A near-term emissions target has been set with SBTi, alongside renewable energy use, energy-efficient lighting and promotion of sustainable transportation and buildings to reduce the carbon footprint|Occupational health and safety practices aligned with ISO 45001:2018|Information-security posture certified to ISO 27001 with SOC 2 Type II attestations, supported by multi-factor authentication and a data-leakage-prevention platform|Policies covering all nine NGRBC principles are in place and have all been approved by the Board, including a Minimum & Living Wages Policy, Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Competition, Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption, Whistleblower, POSH, DEI, Human Rights and Working Conditions, Supplier Code of Conduct, Supplier Risk Assessment and Related Party Transactions policies|Grievance redressal mechanisms exist for every stakeholder group - communities (CSR field visits with NGO partners), shareholders, employees (whistleblower plus HR skip-level meetings), customers (contractual escalation) and value-chain partners; nil complaints filed and nil pending for communities in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25|The Board has formulated a Risk Management Policy under Section 134(3)(n) covering identification, evaluation, monitoring and mitigation of business, operational, financial, regulatory and strategic risks, with a Risk Management Committee among the five Board Committees and a risk statement in Annexure 7|Following its review of the risk landscape, the Board states it has not identified any material risks or perceived threats that would pose a threat to the continued existence of the Company|A Board Diversity Policy has been adopted, with diversity of ethnicity, age, gender, professional expertise and industry experience stated as a key area of strategic focus in Board composition
currentContext.expansion: Saksoft is asset-light and discloses no manufacturing capacity: the BRSR states 'As Saksoft is an IT Services Company, we do not have any Manufacturing plants', with plants shown as Not Applicable and five national offices. Expansion is therefore framed as capability, footprint and platform build-out rather than plant capex. The Board's Report describes investments in a transition 'from people-dependent processes to an AI-driven innovation model', with heavy investment in new AI skill sets and capability frameworks; R&D costs are described as integrated into the operational fabric rather than reported as a separate quantum, and the Company states it has embedded AI across internal HR, recruitment and administration functions with continuous infrastructure upgrades for 24/7 availability and scalability ('platform-centric organization', 'cloud-first infrastructure'). On the environmental side the registered office is housed in a LEED-certified green building; the facilities management (of that building, not the Company itself) 'has recently increased the grid generation capacity through renewable sources to 60% of the overall consumption'; air-conditioning units have been overhauled to eco-friendly gases and refrigerants; and a 158.4KW solar power generation installation has been made at the Noida facility centre - which the report explicitly says is 'owned by the wider group', not by Saksoft Limited. The Group undertakes an annual GHG assessment and has obtained validation of its Near-Term Targets from SBTi for Scope 1, 2 & 3 emission reduction. Notably, the BRSR Principle 2 disclosure reports R&D and capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts as 'Nil' for both FY 2026 and FY 2025. The forward growth ambition disclosed in the stakeholder value-creation spread is acquisition-led: 'Strategic acquisition-led growth with a clear USD 500 Million revenue ambition by 2030', funded without leverage - the Company states it minimises reliance on debt and focuses on 'sustainable growth without borrowing'. Human capital is described as 'around 2,600 plus professionals'.
currentContext.mdna: Management expects the rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence, cloud technologies and data-driven operating models to continue reshaping enterprise technology investments in FY 2026-27|As organisations move from experimentation to enterprise-wide AI deployment, demand is expected to increase for trusted partners capable of delivering secure, scalable and outcome-driven transformation|Enterprises are balancing two priorities simultaneously - remaining competitive in an AI-led market while optimising ongoing technology spend - which is driving vendor consolidation and centralised, AI-enabled operating models|Legacy environments limit the ability to operationalise AI at scale, making modernisation a strategic prerequisite for future growth; the Company cites legacy modernisation as an estimated USD 100 billion in annual enterprise technology spend globally|Rising release velocity and customer expectations are pushing clients from traditional testing towards automation-first QA operations without proportionally higher testing cost|AI is redefining software-engineering economics, creating pressure for faster innovation cycles with controlled engineering investment|Data and security foundations are becoming central to AI competitiveness, with Data, AI and Security initiatives converging into enterprise transformation agendas|The Company cites a Gartner projection that agentic AI will autonomously resolve 80% of common enterprise service interactions by 2029 as the rationale for its VoicePilot investment (third-party forecast, not a company target)|Strong demand continued in the Data, Analytics & AI practice as enterprises invested in modern data platforms, including continued demand for Tableau-to-Power BI migrations and cloud-native analytics adoption|Modernisation, quality-transformation and engineering-led conversations are described as expanding into adjacent cloud, data, AI and managed-services scope, improving account penetration

risks.note: Ranked first in the BRSR material-issues table: external attacks, malware, compromised credentials and business email compromise via phishing may result in data loss and loss of reputation. Mitigated through a mature Information Security Management System, defence-in-depth control architecture, multi-factor authentication, an enhanced data-leakage-prevention platform, encryption and backup/recovery, with ISO 27001 certification and SOC 2 Type II attestations cited as reinforcement. Financial implication flagged negative.

Unauthorised use or disclosure of employee, company or customer data may lead to breach of customer contracts, regulator fines or penalties and reputational damage - a structural exposure for a services firm operating inside client BFS and commerce systems. Mitigation is access control, need-to-know provisioning and regular access reviews. Financial implication flagged negative.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure with concentration in the US geography
risks.note: The Company states it 'operates in the global environment and has maximum business from US geography, hence currency fluctuation is a major risk'. It follows a consistent hedging policy covering most of the net exposure in USD, GBP and Euro, hedged only in India and never beyond 12 months, with gains/losses booked in the revenue line - so a sustained move beyond the 12-month hedge horizon is unhedged. Financial implication flagged negative.

A changing geopolitical landscape in multiple regions (war scenarios) and macroeconomic uncertainty around interest-rate cuts may compress customer discretionary technology spend and reduce opportunities. Mitigation is limited to monitoring and reporting geopolitical risk to the Board's Risk Management Committee. Financial implication flagged negative.

The Company states the risk of attrition 'may hamper long-term sustainability' - the core structural risk of a people-based delivery model. Mitigation is retention and recognition through loyalty and performance award schemes. Financial implication flagged negative.

risks.risk: Business ethics, anti-corruption and whistleblower governance
risks.note: Non-compliance with anti-corruption laws or unethical practices may lead to regulatory penalties, reputational damage and loss of stakeholder trust; separately, the absence of effective reporting mechanisms could leave unethical practices unreported and lead to governance failures. Mitigated through a zero-tolerance Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy, a Code of Conduct with structured training and participation tracking, a Supplier Risk Assessment Checklist for third-party due diligence, and a confidential whistleblower channel with non-retaliation protection.

Well-being (physical, mental and emotional) across employees and the extended workforce is treated as a material issue, with force-majeure events such as medical emergencies and weather-related disruption specifically named. Occupational health and safety practices are stated to be aligned with ISO 45001:2018.

Treated as both risk and opportunity: reducing GHG emissions while building resilience to evolving climate conditions, addressed through renewable energy, energy-efficient lighting, sustainable transportation and buildings, and a near-term target set with SBTi.

one-line thesis: Saksoft crossed INR 1,000 crore revenue in FY26 with robust margin expansion (EBITDA +301 bps YoY) driven by AI-enabled efficiency, though Q4 sequential growth stalled (-0.8%) due to customer decision deferral amid AI uncertainty. The company pivots to outcome-based billing and agent-augmented delivery to decouple headcount from revenue, targeting a $500 million run-rate by 2030 primarily through wallet-share gains in top 20 accounts.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 249cr (Q4, +4% YoY, -0.8% QoQ); FY26 Rev: INR 1,007cr (+14% YoY). EBITDA: INR 45cr (Q4, +24% YoY); Margin: 18.19% (+301 bps YoY). PAT: INR 36cr (Q4, +20% YoY); FY26 PAT: INR 133cr (+23% YoY). Order Book: Pipeline at record USD 25mn (up from USD 5mn six months ago). Net Debt: Net Cash positive INR 223cr. One-offs: None reported; growth impacted by deferred spending from 2 large customers in Q3/Q4.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Aiming for 30% (aggressive) but guiding 14-15% as base case for FY27. Margins: Expect slight compression from current ~18% due to AI investments and contract repricing, though long-term trajectory is upward. Order Inflow: Pipeline strong (USD 25mn) with 6 'big bets' pending conversion. Capex: Minimal; growth funded via internal accruals; no significant capex required for $500mn target.
order book & pipeline: Pipeline stands at USD 25 million (highest in company history, up 5x from USD 5mn six months ago); driven by 6 large 'big bet' opportunities and vendor consolidation proposals offering 25-30% cost savings; conversion delayed by customer caution on AI impact.
segment / subsidiary detail: BFSI (31% of FY26 rev); Emerging Verticals including High-Tech & Telecom (47%); Logistics (14%); Commerce (8%). Geography: Americas (50%), Europe (29%), APAC/Others (21%). Delivery Mix: 56% Offshore, 44% On-site. Customer Concentration: Top 10 clients contribute 58%; Top 20 contribute ~70%.
growth verticals / optionality: 95-98% of growth expected from existing top 20 customers via wallet share expansion (vendor consolidation); inorganic growth via small acquisitions (max INR 100cr target) using internal accruals; transition to outcome-based billing (currently 10%) offers pricing power and margin upside.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margins expanded to 18.57% (FY26) from 16.56%; future margins expected to rise long-term as AI agents replace human headcount (non-linear revenue model), though near-term dip possible due to AI training costs and contract repricing pressures.
capex / expansion: Negligible traditional capex; investment focused on human capital (training developers/PMs in AI/LLMs) and technology accelerators; funded entirely by operating cash flows.
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic growth investments and strategic small-ticket M&A; declared final dividend of 55% (total 100% of face value); maintaining strong net cash balance (INR 223cr) for liquidity and opportunistic deals.
risks & watch-items: Prolonged customer decision deferral due to AI uncertainty; potential cannibalization of T&M revenues by AI agents; margin compression during transition to outcome-based models; competition from GCCs for mid-tier clients; dependency on top 20 clients for 95% of growth.
management quality / tone: Confident in long-term AI-driven structural advantages for nimble players over Tier-1s; candid about near-term growth headwinds (decision delays); aggressive on pipeline quality but cautious on conversion timing; visionary on 'human + agent' hybrid delivery models.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly targets replacing SaaS/Cloud spend with on-prem AI-enabled custom apps to cut customer costs (e.g., $50mn to $25mn reduction); believes AI will level the playing field against Tier-1s by reducing the value of scale; predicts 50-50 human-agent workforce mix by 2030; utilization cap revised to ~85% for humans (agents at 100%).

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Pipeline stands at USD 25 million (highest in company history, up 5x from USD 5mn six months ago); driven by 6 large 'big bet' opportunities and vendor consolidation proposals offering 25-30% cost savings; conversion delayed by customer caution on AI impact.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Aiming for 30% (aggressive) but guiding 14-15% as base case for FY27. Margins: Expect slight compression from current ~18% due to AI investments and contract repricing, though long-term trajectory is upward. Order Inflow: Pipeline strong (USD 25mn) with 6 'big bets' pending conversion. Capex: Minimal; growth funded via internal accruals; no significant capex required for $500mn target.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 95-98% of growth expected from existing top 20 customers via wallet share expansion (vendor consolidation); inorganic growth via small acquisitions (max INR 100cr target) using internal accruals; transition to outcome-based billing (currently 10%) offers pricing power and margin upside.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects the rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence, cloud technologies and data-driven operating models to continue reshaping enterprise technology investments in FY 2026-27
- As organisations move from experimentation to enterprise-wide AI deployment, demand is expected to increase for trusted partners capable of delivering secure, scalable and outcome-driven transformation
- Enterprises are balancing two priorities simultaneously - remaining competitive in an AI-led market while optimising ongoing technology spend - which is driving vendor consolidation and centralised, AI-enabled operating models
- Legacy environments limit the ability to operationalise AI at scale, making modernisation a strategic prerequisite for future growth; the Company cites legacy modernisation as an estimated USD 100 billion in annual enterprise technology spend globally
- Rising release velocity and customer expectations are pushing clients from traditional testing towards automation-first QA operations without proportionally higher testing cost
- AI is redefining software-engineering economics, creating pressure for faster innovation cycles with controlled engineering investment
- Data and security foundations are becoming central to AI competitiveness, with Data, AI and Security initiatives converging into enterprise transformation agendas
- The Company cites a Gartner projection that agentic AI will autonomously resolve 80% of common enterprise service interactions by 2029 as the rationale for its VoicePilot investment (third-party forecast, not a company target)
- Strong demand continued in the Data, Analytics & AI practice as enterprises invested in modern data platforms, including continued demand for Tableau-to-Power BI migrations and cloud-native analytics adoption
- Modernisation, quality-transformation and engineering-led conversations are described as expanding into adjacent cloud, data, AI and managed-services scope, improving account penetration

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margins expanded to 18.57% (FY26) from 16.56%; future margins expected to rise long-term as AI agents replace human headcount (non-linear revenue model), though near-term dip possible due to AI training costs and contract repricing pressures.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing organic growth investments and strategic small-ticket M&A; declared final dividend of 55% (total 100% of face value); maintaining strong net cash balance (INR 223cr) for liquidity and opportunistic deals.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Saksoft is asset-light and discloses no manufacturing capacity: the BRSR states 'As Saksoft is an IT Services Company, we do not have any Manufacturing plants', with plants shown as Not Applicable and five national offices. Expansion is therefore framed as capability, footprint and platform build-out rather than plant capex. The Board's Report describes investments in a transition 'from people-dependent processes to an AI-driven innovation model', with heavy investment in new AI skill sets and capability frameworks; R&D costs are described as integrated into the operational fabric rather than reported as a separate quantum, and the Company states it has embedded AI across internal HR, recruitment and administration functions with continuous infrastructure upgrades for 24/7 availability and scalability ('platform-centric organization', 'cloud-first infrastructure'). On the environmental side the registered office is housed in a LEED-certified green building; the facilities management (of that building, not the Company itself) 'has recently increased the grid generation capacity through renewable sources to 60% of the overall consumption'; air-conditioning units have been overhauled to eco-friendly gases and refrigerants; and a 158.4KW solar power generation installation has been made at the Noida facility centre - which the report explicitly says is 'owned by the wider group', not by Saksoft Limited. The Group undertakes an annual GHG assessment and has obtained validation of its Near-Term Targets from SBTi for Scope 1, 2 & 3 emission reduction. Notably, the BRSR Principle 2 disclosure reports R&D and capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts as 'Nil' for both FY 2026 and FY 2025. The forward growth ambition disclosed in the stakeholder value-creation spread is acquisition-led: 'Strategic acquisition-led growth with a clear USD 500 Million revenue ambition by 2030', funded without leverage - the Company states it minimises reliance on debt and focuses on 'sustainable growth without borrowing'. Human capital is described as 'around 2,600 plus professionals'.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident in long-term AI-driven structural advantages for nimble players over Tier-1s; candid about near-term growth headwinds (decision delays); aggressive on pipeline quality but cautious on conversion timing; visionary on 'human + agent' hybrid delivery models.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": true, "note": "The routed 'RELATED-PARTY TRANSACTIONS' block actually opens with Standalone Note 22(a) Contingent Liabilities, which discloses income-tax matters and states that 'the future cash outflows on items above are determinable only on receipt of the decision or judgment that is pending at various forums and authorities' - i.e. tax proceedings are pending against the Company at multiple forums. The Company adds that it 'does not expect the outcome of these proceedings to have an adverse material effect on the financial results'. No auditor's report, CARO annexure or regulatory-order disclosure is routed to this bundle, so this is the only litigation evidence available here; the flag records that disclosed pending proceedings exist, not that they were assessed material by management.", "as_of": "2026-07-16"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Domain-led delivery with named vertical specialist pools - '400+ Logistics Domain Specialists', '900+ BFS and Fintech Specialists' and '300+ Specialists' in Digital Commerce
- Proprietary accelerators and frameworks reused across engagements (SakMod, UNITE, SakCare, LEAP, Voice BOT, Helsinki, Oslo, Vue Storefront, Commerce Command Centre Framework), which the Company positions as reducing time-to-value and deepening its role in customer transformation journeys
- Consistent operating fundamentals: the COO & CFO states utilisation levels 'have been consistent over the past several years' and attrition 'has remained broadly steady year on year', described as a meaningful competitive differentiator in an industry where talent is both primary asset and primary risk
- Multi-geography delivery and client footprint (United States, Europe, Asia Pacific) enabling integrated, cross-border technology solutions
- Acquisition philosophy framed around acquiring capabilities, talent and entrepreneurial leadership rather than bought revenue, preserving an entrepreneurial operating culture
- Balance-sheet strength cited by the COO & CFO - the year closed with a net cash surplus and an interest coverage ratio in excess of 21 times

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Prolonged customer decision deferral due to AI uncertainty; potential cannibalization of T&M revenues by AI agents; margin compression during transition to outcome-based models; competition from GCCs for mid-tier clients; dependency on top 20 clients for 95% of growth.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly targets replacing SaaS/Cloud spend with on-prem AI-enabled custom apps to cut customer costs (e.g., $50mn to $25mn reduction); believes AI will level the playing field against Tier-1s by reducing the value of scale; predicts 50-50 human-agent workforce mix by 2030; utilization cap revised to ~85% for humans (agents at 100%).

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Six Big Bets framing the next chapter: (1) AI-Powered Shared Services & Unified Command Centre Operations, (2) AI-Led ADMs & Vendor Consolidation, (3) Legacy Modernisation & AI-Readiness Transformation, (4) Autonomous QA Ops & AI-Led Quality Engineering, (5) AI-First Digital Engineering & Future Development Engineering (FDE), (6) DataOps, Data, AI & Security as a Service
- Shift from execution-led engagements to broader transformation ownership - helping customers optimise current operating models while creating capacity for AI-led growth
- Expand wallet share within existing accounts, strengthen …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demand environment] Chairman and Managing Director Mr. Aditya Krishna states that Q1FY27 reflected the continuation of the demand softness which began to be seen towards the third quarter of the last financial year, and that some top clients continue to face near-term pressures.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 66.72%, Public 28.08%, Employee Trust 3.03% and FPI 2.17%.
- [Exceptional items] FY26 shows Exceptional Items of INR 49 Mn (nil in FY24 and FY25), taking PBT to INR 1,796 Mn from INR 1,845 Mn before exceptional items; the deck does not describe their nature.
